whatIsIt.eli5: A tiny helper used only while learning, to judge how likely each point mistake is.
whatIsIt.simple: A small normalising-flow network (6 coupling layers of tiny MLPs) that the RLE keypoint loss uses to measure how likely an error is.
whatIsIt.engineer: 6 affine coupling layers on 2-D residuals; s-nets (Linear 2→64→64→2, Tanh), t-nets (same, no Tanh); log_prob for the RLE loss.

whyExists.eli5: It makes the point grading smarter.
whyExists.simple: Lets the loss learn the real shape of keypoint errors instead of assuming a fixed one.

eli5: Say how likely such a mistake is.
simple: Transforms the 2-D error through 6 small layers.
Computes its log-likelihood under a normal distribution.
engineer: Not executed at inference; its 53,784 params are counted in model.info().
